Pinned by receiving.spec.ts (the ADR 0286 describes).

claim: In recordDoorReceipt the order's delivered_at is written from the event's stored time (factTime.at), never the request's, and only moves forward: the update carries .or(delivered_at.is.null,delivered_at.lt.<the event's time>) so a truck that synced late cannot pull a later truck's time back, and a failed delivered_at write is a 503 with reason order_delivered_at_failed rather than ignored. Pinned by receiving.spec.ts ('a late earlier truck does not move delivered_at back', 'a later truck moves it forward').

claim: Exactly one migration named a_door_receipt_says_which_clock_dated_it adds procurement_receipt_events.occurred_at_basis (text, nullable, no default) with two CHECKs: procurement_receipt_events_occurred_at_basis_check (NULL or one of 'sent', 'back_dated', 'server', the same three values as FACT_TIME_BASES in apps/api-gateway/src/common/fact-time.ts) and procurement_receipt_events_occurred_at_basis_has_evidence (a sent or back_dated row carries client_captured_at). No CHECK compares occurred_at with created_at (ADR 0286 option 6). Proven on a local Postgres 17 built from every migration on main plus this one (sim-run fixes pgtest.sh lane, 2026-10-04): a sent or back_dated row without client_captured_at and an unknown basis are refused with 23514, a server row with no occurred_at equals created_at, and the same test fails on a build without the migration. That proof is not in CI: the test is p4-scratch/sim-run/fixes/audits/doortime-occurred-at-basis_test.sql, outside the repo because the PR is at the 15-file cap, so only someone with that file can re-run it. What CI re-checks is this row, statically: the column, the two CHECKs' text, and the column comment, which must say that a clamped sent row is dated by the gateway's receipt of a clock up to five minutes ahead and that NULL also marks rows the door does not write (verifyReceipt's reconciled events). [2026-10-06: the comment clauses were added to this verify.]

claim: The door's stock movement is dated at the fact's time: the apply_stock_movement call in recordDoorReceipt (receiving.service.ts, the rpc keyed door-receipt:{eventId}) passes p_occurred_at: factTime.at, the event's stored time (on a retry, the first attempt's). apply_stock_movement (migration a_pos_sale_is_dated_by_its_check, ADR 0281) dates the ledger row LEAST(COALESCE(p_occurred_at, now()), now()), so a late-synced receipt lands on its real day in the stock ledger as it does in the event and the order. Only the ledger row's transaction_date moves: the purchase lot keeps inventory_lots.received_at at DEFAULT now(). Pinned by receiving.spec.ts (four [REVERT-FAILS] cases in the ADR 0286 describe assert p_occurred_at; all four fail with the argument removed, measured 2026-10-06). Resolved 2026-10-06; it was open until then because the call did not pass the argument. tech-debt.d/2026-10-04-fix-door-keeps-the-arrival-time.md.

claim: POST /providers/:id/retroactive-order dates an order by the ADR 0286 rule: ProvidersController.createRetroactiveOrder or ProvidersService.createRetroactiveOrder passes dto.invoiceDate through resolveFactTime with the token's role before createOrder writes it. OPEN: today the service passes dto.invoiceDate straight on as alreadyFulfilled.deliveredAt (providers/providers.service.ts:1201), and createOrder writes it to the new DELIVERED order's requested_at and delivered_at (procurement/procurement.service.ts:1236, :1284-1288). The DTO checks it only as an optional string (providers/dto/retroactive-order.dto.ts:95), and the route reads no role, so any signed-in member of the house can date an order at any time, with no 72-hour line and no back-dated mark. No web or mobile client calls the route today. Found by the review of f534823e0 (2026-10-06), which corrected ADR 0286's sentence that no order write accepts a sent time.
